content:
anya: quick signal from the vanguard-q canary — funcall JSON parse failures spiked after the encoder-int8 build rolled today
anya: failure rate ~2.3% on canary traffic (was ~0.2% on baseline) :eyes:
mike: ugh. any pattern in the payloads? truncated arrays, bad escaping, control chars?
anya: looking like stray non-printable bytes in the toolcall suffix. example from logs: 
```
INVOKE_RESP: {
  \"tool\": \"lookup\",
  \"args\": {
    \"q\": \"price\",
    \"loc\": \"SF\"
  }
}\u0000
```
mike: that trailing \u0000 definitely will break strict json parse in our toolhook
sam: do we know if it's tokenizer/encoder or runtime streaming boundary?
anya: hypothesis: int8 quantization changed byte->token alignment for some unicode sequences; streaming runtime then emits a zero-byte sentinel at end of chunk that used to be swallowed
lia: can we reproduce locally with the same seed + prompt?
anya: yes. repro script: `scripts/repro/canary_vanguard_q.sh` (added small harness) —produces ~3/200 malformed outputs in my run
ci-bot: build 2026-03-23-18 passed unit tests, deployed to canary pool 3 at 18:22 UTC
mike: short-term mitigation: add a sanitizer step before parse that removes 0x00 and other control chars. also relax the strict-parser fallback to try a repair pass (json5 tolerant)
sam: we should avoid masking root cause though. plan: 1) add sanitizer in canary pipeline 2) run tokenization diff vs baseline to find offending sequences 3) run micro-bisect over quant params (per-channel scale vs symmetric)
anya: doing 1) now — deploying sanitizer transformer (strip control chars, normalize NFKC) to 10% of canary traffic
lia: can you post the exact regex/transform you used? will add to eval harness
anya: transformer snippet: `payload = re.sub(r"[\\x00-\\x08\\x0B-\\x0C\\x0E-\\x1F]", "", payload)`
mike: also add a postfix wrapper to outputs for toolcalls: wrap JSON in a known sentinel like `---REDWOOD-JSON-START---` / `---END---` so streaming boundaries don't get mixed with content for a quick compatibility guard
sam: that wrapper will require small client and runtime changes but easy on canary only
lia: experiment idea: run token-level diff between int8 and fp16 decodes for failing prompts and search for the first token that differs, then inspect its bytes pre-tokenizer
anya: collecting diffs now; streaming a sample to S3: s3://redwood-canaries/vanguard-q/1716334567/diffs.jsonl
ci-bot: canary deployment 1716334567-sanitizer rolled to 10% at 19:01 UTC
anya: after sanitizer roll: parse failure rate dropped to 0.4% on the sanitized cohort (vs 2.3% before) — not perfect but good signal
mike: good. next run: run a micro-quant sweep toggling symmetric/asymmetric and per-channel scales. target is parity to baseline within 0.2% parse fail
sam: i'll set up the sweep grid, include temperature and kvprefix-length as covariates
lia: add an evaluation probe that runs strict-schema checks (schema: tool:lookup args{q:string,loc:string}) and records repair-actions (strip, wrap, json5-repair) as tags
anya: logged an issue: RED-ML-1279 with repro details, sample IDs, and links to diffs + failed payloads
ci-bot: RED-ML-1279 created by anya at 19:12 UTC
mike: owners?
anya: i'll own triage + sanitizer follow-up. sam will run quant sweep. lia will add schema telemetry to the harness
sam: ETA for first sweep pass: EOD tomorrow
lia: I'll push the schema telemetry change in a small PR and wire it to the canary metrics dashboard
anya: provisional mitigation timeline: keep sanitizer + wrapper in canary until we get quant config that matches baseline; if sweep results are clear, roll to dedicated for a slow rollout
mike: also add alert that triggers if parse_fail_rate > 1% sustained for 15m on any canary pool
anya: added alert in console: name \"canary-funcall-parse-fail-rate\" threshold 1% 15m
sam: thanks — will follow up with sweep results, posting to this thread
lia: thanks everyone, nice triage. :thumbsup:
anya: noted next check-in 36h or earlier if regression worsens
